turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come through, I'll check your obs quickly before Dr. Hughes sees you. How are you travelling?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit all over the place, honestly. I'm pregnant and I've started spotting with some cramps, so I'm anxious. I reckon I'm somewhere between eight and ten weeks but I can't pin the dates.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Alright. Blood pressure is 122 over 76, pulse 88, temperature 36.6, oxygen saturation 98 percent. All looking fine. Have a seat.

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that blood pressure okay? I've been on pregnancy forums and they talk about high blood pressure with spotting meaning all sorts of scary things. My partner is waiting just outside. I told him to hang back so I could explain everything first.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Those readings are perfectly normal. The doctor's on the way.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hi there, I'm Dr. Hughes. Come and sit. I hear you're early in pregnancy with some spotting. Can you walk me through it from the start?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, um, so about three weeks ago I did a home pregnancy test from the chemist. The line was faint the first time, so I did another the next morning and it was clearly positive. Saw my GP about ten days ago and the blood test confirmed the pregnancy. Then the spotting started three days ago, light brown, just a smear on the toilet paper when I wipe, not enough for a liner, and it hasn't increased.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the cramps? Any other symptoms you've noticed?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Cramps low down in my pelvis, mild, a dull ache like a period but gentler. They come four or five times a day, each lasting about ten minutes, and lying down with a heat pack settles them. I've got morning nausea but I haven't vomited at all. Breasts have been tender for weeks, I'm exhausted and falling asleep early, no dizziness.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): How sure are you of the dates of your last period?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Not sure at all. The last period was around Diwali, or after. Diwali was late October, we went to my parents' in Melbourne for the celebrations, and I think the bleeding was that week or the week after I got home, but I never logged it. Work was flat out, I'm a year four teacher and the concert rehearsals were every arvo, so maybe eight weeks, maybe ten, maybe less.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll leave the dates uncertain. Any heavier bleeding, clots, severe pain, shoulder pain, or feeling faint?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none of those. Spotting has stayed light, no clots. Pain is only mild. No shoulder pain and I haven't felt faint or dizzy once.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about medicines or supplements?

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I take Elevit, one tablet every morning. For the cramps I've used paracetamol, two 500 mg tablets which is one gram, yesterday afternoon and again this morning. I also take vitamin D 1000 units a couple of times a week, because a blood test two years ago, they said it was borderline, so I was told to supplement, but I forget a lot.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): First pregnancy? Any past operations or ongoing illnesses?

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): This is my first pregnancy. I had an appendicectomy at sixteen, keyhole, no problems after. No ongoing illnesses, no thyroid issues or high blood pressure or anything. I am very anxious though because my sister had a miscarriage at twelve weeks last year after spotting started, and I haven't slept properly for three nights.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm sorry, that family history would weigh on anyone. Coming in today is the right step.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Can my partner join us? He's just outside and getting more worried the longer he waits. I know I give too much detail but I'd rather you hear it all.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Absolutely, let's have him in.
[SEG0021] person_1 (NURSE): I'll bring him through now.

[SEG0022] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): G'day doctor. Thanks. She's been really anxious since the spotting showed up a few days back. Barely anything there when I looked, but her sister's miscarriage has her spooked.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I did tell you it was light. I haven't been hiding how much it is.

[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): It helps to hear it from both of you. The old vitamin D result isn't relevant to today's problem. I'd like an ultrasound scan today and blood tests, specifically a quantitative hCG, full blood count, progesterone, and we can add vitamin D.

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Doing it today is such a relief. I keep reading that if the dates are earlier than I think, the scan might not show a heartbeat yet and then you have to wait and worry all over again. My GP never gave me the actual number from the last hCG, just that it was positive, which makes it harder to know if it's rising.

[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll interpret the scan alongside the uncertain dates, so an early scan without a heartbeat isn't automatically bad news. The bloods today give us proper numbers to follow.
[SEG0027] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): If the bleeding gets heavier tonight, what do we do?

[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come straight to the emergency department if you soak a pad in an hour, pass big clots, the pain becomes severe, or you feel faint, dizzy or get shoulder pain. Otherwise rest, drink plenty of fluids, and I'll see you back here in two days to go over the results. Ring or return sooner if the worry gets too much.

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Two days works. I think I'll stay home from school tomorrow, I won't be any use to the kids. Can I keep taking the Elevit and paracetamol the same way? I'll skip the vitamin D so it doesn't affect the level, and I've also been a bit constipated this past week, nothing major, just not going as often, probably from the iron.

[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, continue Elevit daily and paracetamol at the dose you've used when you need it. Hold the vitamin D until after the blood test. For the constipation, more water and some prunes usually do the trick. You don't need strict bed rest, just take it easy.

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Prunes it is, my mum always says that. I should also mention I had a urine infection a year ago, it burned when I went to the toilet, antibiotics cleared it, and I have no urinary symptoms now. Is the exhaustion normal as well? I like to tell you every detail so nothing gets missed.

[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): The old infection sounds long gone and no symptoms now is reassuring. Tiredness is very common this early, especially with the poor sleep and worry on top. I think we've got the important points.
[SEG0033] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is there a chance it could be ectopic? You asked about shoulder pain so I wondered. She hasn't had that.

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ectopic pregnancy is something we consider whenever there's spotting and cramps early on, but your mild symptoms make it less likely. The scan should show us where the pregnancy is. My impression at this stage is that this may be a threatened miscarriage or simply common early spotting, with the dates still uncertain. We won't know which until the tests come back.

[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Threatened miscarriage sounds frightening. Does that mean the pregnancy is probably ending? I really hope it's just ordinary spotting. I've been so worried I can barely think straight at work.

[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): No, it doesn't mean that. Many pregnancies continue perfectly well after some spotting. The word threatened just flags that we need to check. Try to step away from the internet tonight if you can help it.
[SEG0037] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We'll keep her off Google. So bloods and scan this afternoon, then back in two days unless something changes.

[SEG0038] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print the forms and walk you down to pathology. They should get the ultrasound done this afternoon as well if we send the request now. The return advice is on the discharge note too.

[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. I feel a little less panicked having it all booked for today. I'll do the fluids and the prunes and rest on the couch. Um, one last thing, the heat pack is okay to keep using on my tummy, isn't it, not too hot?
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, a warm heat pack is fine, just not hot enough to burn, and not for hours on end. See you in two days. Come sooner for any of those warning signs we talked about.
[SEG0041] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Cheers. We'll head down now. Thanks for fitting us in.
